prompt: Edit this exact image for a German Bildungshaus website. Preserve the four crooked crayon people holding hands and the flower: same expressions, lines, imperfect anatomy, colors and handmade white-paper feel. Add only a simple small Bildungshaus building BEHIND the people in the background, visible between/behind their heads: a wonky rectangular house with a crooked orange triangular roof, 3 uneven blue windows and an open door. It must look drawn by the same 5-year-old, naive, flat, very sparse, no architectural perspective or beautiful precise lines. Building is secondary, lighter pencil pressure, does not cover or replace people or dominate. No writing, no letters, no frame. Keep image landscape and generous white paper. Do not idealize the original drawing.

Create one landscape crayon drawing on plain white paper, as actually drawn by an impulsive 5-year-old: crooked, wildly uneven outlines, mismatched proportions, sparse messy pencil scribbling, empty white areas. Scene for a German Bildungshaus website: three small children at a wonky lunch table looking toward an adult cook in a lopsided white chef hat. The cook is gently overwhelmed juggling a wooden spoon and a big pot, raised zigzag eyebrows, a few tiny stress strokes, kind not angry or threatening. One child points toward a plate, another raises their hand, an adult colleague at the edge offers help. A few simple carrots/green peas on plates, nothing detailed. Warm human everyday comedy without mockery. Main blue and burnt-orange crayons plus green and graphite. Flat child drawing, NOT a polished children's-book illustration, NOT vector, no shading, no coherent perspective, no text or symbols that need reading. More crooked and primitive than an adult pretending to draw a child picture. Widely spaced subjects, landscape 3:2.

A single small square naive crayon doodle by a fairly careful 6-year-old on pure white paper: a very lopsided transparent jam jar with three oversized wonky yellow-orange round coins inside and two loose coins beside it. A tiny blue uneven house mark drawn on one coin, no letters or numbers. Sparse blue and burnt-orange pencil strokes and a little yellow, visible paper, very simple shapes, coin circles imperfect, jar tilted, inconsistent sizes. Emotional idea: small resources can help make a shared place. No currency sign, no stock-market arrows, no polished vector art, no intricate details, no shiny realism, no border. Keep at least one quarter of the canvas empty around the drawing.
